item.title: Introducing Moraine: DuckLake entirely in object storage, no catalog service required
item.description: Moraine moves the DuckLake catalog into object storage, removing the need for a separate catalog service.
item.content:encoded:
We’re excited to introduce you to Moraine, which moves your DuckLake catalog to object storage right alongside your data. That means you don’t need to host a separate Postgres or DuckDB/Quack server for each data lake.

We built it when faced with hosting tenant-scoped data warehouses for our analytics clients at Contour. We first moved to DuckLake to avoid commercial data warehouse costs (and because it’s a great spec), but the Postgres hosting for each lake also got expensive, even though it sat idle most of the time. Moraine fixes exactly that. An idle lake costs just object storage. And, spinning up a new, separate lake is as simple as picking a new S3 bucket or prefix.

In Moraine, the catalog lives in SlateDB, an LSM-based key-value store that stores the catalog in object storage alongside your data. That means a commit is a single object write and there’s no separate service to run. SlateDB is a database, so we can maintain DuckLake’s transactional properties and inline small data changes. With proper tuning, write and read performance is competitive with DuckLake on Postgres.

There are a couple of drawbacks to our approach: only one process can attach read-write per lake at a time, with others limited to read only. And, attach times are slower than the other catalogs. If you have one ingest service and many readers (our use case) this works well. If you need lots of independent writers, it may not be a good fit.

We’ve also used SlateDB’s key-value storage to add native indexes to DuckLake. Just like in stock DuckDB, run CREATE INDEX on a column and the index is kept in step with every commit, so lookups by that column read only the files that hold it.

Moraine is still alpha-quality software, though we’ve started putting it through its paces with production clients. For more on how to get started, see Getting started. Dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0. A big thank you to the developers of DuckDB and SlateDB for the building blocks.

Feedback welcome, especially on workloads and use cases where Moraine breaks down. Open an issue or start a thread in Discussions. We can’t wait to see what you build with it!
